name: Isaac Boro’s Niger Delta Republic

actors.name: Niger Delta Volunteer Force (Isaac Boro, Sam Owonaro, Nottingham Dick)

summary.text: Isaac Adaka Boro, an Ijaw born at Oloibiri, where oil was first struck, was a former policeman and student leader at Nsukka who wanted the Ijaw to control the Delta’s oil. After the coup of January 1966 he trained young men from the Ijaw clans as the Niger Delta Volunteer Force behind his father’s compound at Kaiama, and on 23 February 1966 proclaimed a Niger Delta Republic. It held out for twelve days before soldiers under Ojukwu, the East’s military governor, captured Boro and his comrades, who were tried for treason. Gowon pardoned them in May 1967. Boro joined the federal army as a major and was killed near Okrika on 9 May 1968. Ken Saro-Wiwa, the Ijaw youth movements and later Delta militants all claimed him.

moments.title: The Niger Delta Republic
moments.text: Boro proclaims the republic; his volunteers had trained behind his father’s compound at Kaiama.

moments.title: Twelve days, then capture
moments.text: After twelve days the rising is put down; Boro and his comrades are taken by soldiers under Ojukwu and charged with treason.

moments.title: Pardoned
moments.text: Gowon’s government grants them amnesty shortly before the civil war.

moments.title: Boro killed
moments.text: Now a federal major, Boro dies on active duty near Ogu, close to Okrika, in unclear circumstances.

reviewNotes: The area of the rising is approximate: Kaiama and the creeks around Yenagoa.
